accepted_interpretation.interpretation: A finite certificate and an asymptotic theorem cover complementary height regimes. The junction parameter R compresses that coverage into a single all-height hypothesis usable by an existing explicit-formula proof.

accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: The span directly supports the verified height H, the Kadiri comparison, the choice B=17 and R=6.455, the t>=24 zero-free region, and the stated theta/psi bounds. No material imported theorem content appears beyond the source's own citations; the phrase all-height hypothesis should be read only for the stated t>=24 region. The bridge language adds a specific dependency relation rather than merely renaming a representation, so style-only risk is low.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: With RH verified to H=3.061×10^10, the source solves H=exp(R log 17/(R−5.69693)) and takes R=6.455. This yields a zero-free region for t≥24 and then explicit error envelopes |θ(x)−x|≤xε0(x) for x≥149 and |ψ(x)−x|≤xε0(x) for x≥23.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: The construction does not optimize R and B jointly and does not rederive Schoenfeld's numerical estimates; it deliberately keeps B fixed so those estimates remain reusable. The displayed constants and square-root/exponential placement are formula-sensitive, although this unit's extraction is legible; numerical reuse should still be checked against the PDF. Describing R as a junction parameter and the combined inputs as complementary height regimes is a reasonable conceptual compression of the displayed comparison. The formulas are legible but decimal constants, logarithm placement, and the nested square root in epsilon_0 remain PDF-sensitive.

parents.title: Partial summation turns a theta error into a pi minus li bound with a computable splice point

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Source fact: identity (8) rewrites π(x)−li(x) as an endpoint term in θ(x)−x plus a weighted integral of θ(t)−t and fixed lower-end terms. Interpretation: this gives a one-way transfer of a pointwise θ-error bound to the π scale; it does not preserve or invert all information in the θ error. The large range is discharged by an antiderivative majorant g, while the low range is reduced to prime intervals: because π is constant and li increases on [p_k,p_{k+1}), li(x)−π(x) is largest at the next-prime endpoint (as an endpoint bound), leaving finitely many reported checks. The gain is a clean analytic/discrete splice; the remaining burden is the formula-sensitive majorization and the unpreserved computations.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Decomposes the proof into an analytic one-way error transfer and a discrete monotonic endpoint test, and identifies constancy of π together with increase of li—not generic information preservation—as the mechanism that compresses the low range.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted after replacing the critic-flagged preservation claim with the actual one-way inequality and making interval-endpoint monotonicity explicit. Formula extraction is sensitive around the exponents and square-root exponential, and no executable artifact is supplied, so computational reproducibility remains outside this unit.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The span displays (8), chooses α=7/5 so that g′ dominates ε₀(t)/(log t)² for t≥149, takes x₀=10^8, and reports a Mathematica evaluation yielding (9) for x≥10^8. It then invokes Kotnik's π(x)<li(x) result through 10^14 and (10), and reports verification for k≥48, equivalently x≥229.
